lessons.title: Past: खाया/खाई
lessons.learn: Past agrees GENDER! Boy: खाया (ate), girl: खाई! वह गया (he went), वह गई (she went). था/थी = was: मैं खुश था (I was happy — boy)! And कल = yesterday AND tomorrow — tense decides!

grammar.title: Root + या/यी · था/थी
grammar.explain: खा→खाया (m), खा→खाई (f). गया/गई (went), पढ़ा/पढ़ी (read). था (was-m), थी (was-f): वह खुश थी (she was happy)!
mistakes: Girls saying खाया — girls say खाई!
Saying कल गया for tomorrow — कल + past = yesterday, कल + future = tomorrow!

lessons.title: Future: खाऊँगा/खाएगा
lessons.learn: Future sings -गा! मैं खाऊँगा (I will eat — boy), मैं खाऊँगी (girl), वह खाएगा (he will eat), आप खाएँगे (you will eat)! कल + future = tomorrow!

grammar.title: -ऊँगा/-एगा/-एगी/-एँगे
grammar.explain: मैं खाऊँगा (m), मैं खाऊँगी (f), वह खाएगा (m), वह खाएगी (f), हम खाएँगे (we will eat)! Root + vowel + गा/गी!
mistakes: Saying हम खाएगा — हम takes खाएँगे!

lessons.title: कल — yesterday and tomorrow in one word
lessons.learn: कल is both yesterday and tomorrow; the verb decides which one you mean. कल मैं बाज़ार गया था = yesterday I went; कल मैं बाज़ार जाऊँगा = tomorrow I will go. The same is true of परसों (the day before yesterday / the day after tomorrow), so a Hindi sentence about time is carried by its verb.

vocab.en: day before yesterday / day after tomorrow

grammar.title: Time words carry no tense — the verb does
grammar.explain: Hindi does not mark कल as past or future. A perfective verb (गया, खाया, आया) sends it backwards; a future verb (जाऊँगा, खाऊँगा, आऊँगा) sends it forwards. Put the time word first in the sentence and the listener hears the direction from the ending.
grammar.pattern: कल + गया/गई/गया था = yesterday · कल + जाऊँगा/जाएगी = tomorrow

examples.en: I will go to Delhi tomorrow.

examples.t: परसों बारिश हुई थी, और परसों फिर होगी।
examples.r: parsõ bāriś huī thī, aur parsõ phir hogī.
examples.en: It rained the day before yesterday, and it will rain again the day after tomorrow.

mistakes: कल मैं बाज़ार जाऊँगा था — a future form and a past marker cannot sit together; choose one direction.
Putting कल at the end of the sentence: Hindi time words normally open it, and a late कल sounds like an afterthought.

dialogue.en: Did you go to the market yesterday?

dialogue.t: नहीं, कल मैं घर पर थी। बाज़ार मैं परसों गई थी।
dialogue.r: nahī̃, kal main ghar par thī. bāzār main parsõ gaī thī.
dialogue.en: No, yesterday I was at home. I went to the market the day before yesterday.

dialogue.t: अच्छा। तो कल फिर जाना है?
dialogue.r: acchā. to kal phir jānā hai?
dialogue.en: I see. So we have to go again tomorrow?

dialogue.t: हाँ, कल सुबह जाऊँगी। आप भी चलिए।
dialogue.r: hā̃, kal subah jāū̃gī. āp bhī calie.
dialogue.en: Yes, I will go tomorrow morning. Come along.

practice.q: कल मैं स्कूल गया। — when did this happen?
कल मैं बाज़ार ____। (I will go tomorrow)
I went to Delhi yesterday.

practice.answer: I will go to Delhi tomorrow.

practice.q: Which word can mean both yesterday and tomorrow?
Match the time word with the day it names.
practice.answer: परसों = the day before yesterday or the day after tomorrow
options: परसों = the day before yesterday or the day after tomorrow

— आप कल कहाँ थे? — ____ (I was at home yesterday.)
Explain the difference: कल मैं आया। / कल मैं आऊँगा।
practice.answer: The first is yesterday and the second is tomorrow; कल itself carries no direction.

practice.q: Write three sentences about yesterday, today and tomorrow using कल once only.
practice.answer: कल मैं दफ़्तर गया था। आज मैं घर पर हूँ। कल मैं स्कूल जाऊँगा।

quiz.why: जाऊँगा is future, so कल means tomorrow.

options: the day before yesterday or the day after tomorrow
quiz.why: परसों is two days away in either direction.
Past needs a perfective plus था; the others mix forms.

quiz.q: Where does a time word usually sit in a Hindi sentence?
options: Before the verb, after the object
quiz.why: Hindi sentences normally open with place or time, then the subject.

lessons.title: को/से/का + मुझे
lessons.learn: Hindi's glue words come AFTER! को (to), से (from/with), का/की/के (of — agrees!): मेरा घर (my house), मेरी किताब (my book)! मुझे = to-me: मुझे पानी चाहिए (I need water)!

grammar.title: को · से · का/की/के
grammar.explain: मुझको = मुझे (to me)! घर को (to the house), घर से (from home), घर का (of the house). का (m), की (f), के (m-pl)!

lessons.title: में/पर + कहाँ/किधर
lessons.learn: BEING vs GOING! में (in), पर (on). कहाँ? = where (being), किधर? = which way (going)! मैं दिल्ली में रहता हूँ (I live in Delhi). स्कूल किधर है? = Which way is school?

grammar.title: में/पर · कहाँ/किधर

mistakes: Saying में for ON — on = पर!

lessons.title: ने — the marker of who did it
lessons.learn: When a verb is transitive and finished, the doer takes ने: मैंने चाय पी, उसने खाना बनाया. The verb then agrees with the thing acted on, not with the doer — उसने दो किताबें पढ़ीं. Intransitive verbs never take it: मैं स्कूल गया, never मैंने स्कूल गया.

vocab.en: doer marker with finished transitive verbs
I (as doer of a finished action)

grammar.title: doer + ने + object + perfective verb
grammar.explain: ने marks the doer only in the perfective, and only for transitive verbs. The verb drops its agreement with the doer and follows the object instead: मैंने एक किताब पढ़ी (feminine object), मैंने दो किताबें पढ़ीं (plural), मैंने पानी पिया (masculine object).

examples.en: I drank tea in the morning.

mistakes: मैंने जयपुर गया — जाना is intransitive, so there is no ने: मैं जयपुर गया।
मैंने किताब पढ़ा — the verb agrees with किताब, so it is पढ़ी: मैंने किताब पढ़ी।

dialogue.t: नहीं, मैंने अख़बार नहीं पढ़ा। मैंने एक किताब पढ़ी।
dialogue.r: nahī̃, mainne akhbār nahī̃ paṛhā. mainne ek kitāb paṛhī.
dialogue.en: No, I did not read the newspaper. I read a book.

dialogue.t: यह किताब प्रेमचंद ने लिखी थी।
dialogue.r: yah kitāb Premcand ne likhī thī.

practice.answer: The first verb is intransitive so there is no ने; the second is transitive and perfective, so ने is required.

practice.answer: मैं स्कूल गया। मैंने होमवर्क किया और मैंने चाय पी।

lessons.title: पसंद and चाहिए
lessons.learn: LIKES flip! मुझे चाय पसंद है = To-me tea is pleasing = I like tea. NEEDS too: मुझे पानी चाहिए = I need water. The THING decides है/हैं: मुझे किताबें पसंद हैं!

grammar.title: मुझे X पसंद है · मुझे X चाहिए
grammar.explain: मुझे चाय पसंद है (I like tea), मुझे पानी चाहिए (I need water). Plural things: मुझे किताबें पसंद हैं!
mistakes: Saying मैं पसंद हूँ — likes: मुझे…पसंद है!
Saying मुझे किताबें पसंद है — plural: पसंद हैं!

lessons.title: Shopping: कितने का
lessons.learn: Shop in Hindi! कितने का है? (How much?), महँगा (expensive), सस्ता (cheap). Money: रुपया (rupee). मैं लेता हूँ = I'll take it (boy)!

grammar.title: कितने का है? + मैं लेता हूँ
grammar.explain: रोटी कितने की है? (how much is the bread — f: की!). सौ रुपये (100 rupees). मैं लेता हूँ = I'll take it (boy), मैं लेती हूँ (girl)!
grammar.pattern: कितने का/की है? · मैं लेता/लेती हूँ
mistakes: Saying रोटी कितने का — रोटी (f): कितने की!
Girls saying लेता हूँ — girls: लेती हूँ!

dialogue.t: महँगा है! पनीर कितने का है?
dialogue.r: mahṅgā hai! panīr kitne kā hai?
dialogue.en: It's expensive! How much is the cheese?

lessons.title: रेस्टोरेंट में — ordering and the bill
lessons.learn: Two verbs run a Hindi restaurant: दीजिए (please give) and लाइए (please bring). मुझे एक थाली दीजिए asks for a plate for yourself; उन्हें मेन्यू लाइए brings the menu to them. To close the meal you ask for the बिल or, more traditionally, the हिसाब.

grammar.title: मुझे … दीजिए · उन्हें … लाइए
grammar.explain: The person who receives takes को — मुझे, हमें, उन्हें — and the request verb comes last with the respectful इए ending. देना → दीजिए (give), लाना → लाइए (bring), दिखाना → दिखाइए (show). Degree words sit before the noun: थोड़ा कम तीखा, बहुत मीठा.
grammar.pattern: मुझे + चीज़ + दीजिए · थोड़ा कम/ज़्यादा + तीखा/मीठा

examples.t: थोड़ा कम तीखा बनाइए, और अंत में बिल लाइए।
examples.r: thoṛā kam tīkhā banāie, aur ant meṅ bil lāie.
examples.en: Please make it a little less spicy, and bring the bill at the end.

mistakes: मैं चाय चाहता हूँ दीजिए — two request patterns in one sentence. Choose मुझे चाय दीजिए or मुझे चाय चाहिए.
लीजिए (please take) is not लाइए (please bring). The second is what you say in a restaurant.

dialogue.t: ज़रा मेन्यू दिखाइए। और मुझे एक थाली दीजिए।
dialogue.r: zarā menyū dikhāie. aur mujhe ek thālī dījie.
dialogue.en: Please show me the menu. And give me one plate.
All right. Shall I keep it less spicy?

dialogue.t: हाँ, थोड़ा कम तीखा। और खाने के बाद बिल लाइए।
dialogue.r: hā̃, thoṛā kam tīkhā. aur khāne ke bād bil lāie.
dialogue.en: Yes, a little less spicy. And bring the bill after the meal.

practice.q: You want the menu brought to you. Which do you say?
मुझे एक थाली ____। (please give)
Please bring the bill.
मुझे एक थाली दीजिए।
Which word means ‘the account’ in a restaurant?
Match the request verb with its meaning.
Put these in order: लाइए · बिल · ज़रा
Build the request: ‘Please make it a little less spicy.’
Find the mistake: मुझे चाय दीजिए चाहिए।
— खाना कैसा है? — ____ (It is very good, but it is a little too spicy.)
practice.answer: बहुत अच्छा है, लेकिन थोड़ा ज़्यादा तीखा है।

practice.q: Order a meal for two and ask for the bill.
practice.answer: हमें दो थाली दीजिए, और ज़रा मेन्यू दिखाइए। खाने के बाद बिल लाइए।

practice.q: मीरा ने थाली ली, चाय पी और बिल माँगा। What did Meera do, in order?
practice.answer: She took a plate, drank tea, and asked for the bill.

quiz.why: लाना → लाइए. लीजिए would be ‘please take’.

quiz.q: मुझे एक थाली दीजिए — who receives the plate?
To ask for the bill you say…
quiz.why: The bill is brought to you, so लाइए.
The degree word comes before the adjective: थोड़ा कम + तीखा.

quiz.q: Which sentence mixes two patterns and is wrong?
quiz.why: चाहता हूँ and दीजिए are two different requests and cannot share a sentence.

culture.text: होली Holi is a spring festival, and it is also the most useful vocabulary lesson in the calendar. The night before is होलिका दहन holikā dahan, a bonfire; the day itself is रंग rāng, colour, thrown as dry गुलाल gulāl powder or shot from a पिचकारी pichkārī, a water syringe. Strangers are fair game and the greeting is बुरा न मानो, होली है — ‘don’t take offence, it is Holi’.

reading.text: सुबह आठ बजे हैं। मैं बाज़ार जाता हूँ। बाज़ार में बहुत भीड़ है। मैं दो किलो आलू और एक किलो टमाटर खरीदता हूँ। दुकानदार कहता है, “पचास रुपये।” मैं कहता हूँ, “थोड़ा कम कर दीजिए।” वह हँसता है और कहता है, “ठीक है, पैंतालीस।” मैं घर वापस आता हूँ और चाय बनाता हूँ।
reading.gloss: It is eight in the morning. I go to the market. The market is very crowded. I buy two kilos of potatoes and one kilo of tomatoes. The shopkeeper says, “Fifty rupees.” I say, “Make it a little less.” He laughs and says, “Fine, forty-five.” I come back home and make tea.

listening.script:
— भैया, यह कुर्ता कितने का है?
— चार सौ रुपये, दीदी।
— चार सौ? बहुत ज़्यादा है। तीन सौ में दीजिए।
— नहीं दीदी, तीन सौ पचास का है। आप के लिए तीन सौ बीस।
— ठीक है, पैक कर दीजिए।
listening.gloss:
— Brother, how much is this kurta?
— Four hundred rupees, sister.
— Four hundred? That is too much. Give it for three hundred.
— No, sister, it costs me three hundred fifty. For you, three hundred twenty.
— Fine, pack it.

idioms.meaning: it will do, it is good enough — the shrug that ends an argument about quality
for no reason, nothing special — the answer to क्यों?
nice one! — genuine appreciation of something clever
see you — the normal goodbye, with no date attached
relax, there is no rush — also a polite way to stall a request
whatever you prefer — the polite deferral when you disagree
hold on a moment — used on the phone and at counters, never literally a minute

idioms.literal: it is not known to me
idioms.meaning: I don’t know — the honest answer; add माफ़ कीजिए to soften it
a bit — the standard understatement for ‘I know some of that language’
one or another, somehow — when you cannot name who or how

mistakes.why: Hindi has no verb ‘to have’. Possession is the postposition पास plus होना: ‘a book is near me’.
a place needs its postposition. घर takes में inside; in a sentence like ‘I read at home’ in English the preposition comes first, in Hindi it comes after the noun.

mistakes.wrong: पचास रुपये का है? (asking the price of many items)
mistakes.right: पचास रुपये का है? / पचास रुपये की हैं?
mistakes.why: का-के-की agrees with the thing being priced, not with the money. One masculine item: का. A feminine or plural item: की.

task.title: One market conversation, both roles
task.instructions: Copy the bargaining dialogue out by hand, then act both sides aloud. Change three things: the item, the first price, and the final price. Keep the phrases पैक कर दीजिए, कितने का है and थोड़ा कम कर दीजिए exactly as they are — those three carry most of the bargaining, and the numbers are the easy part.
